"""On-policy Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT).

Each step samples contexts, rolls out the *student's own* response, then
minimizes the exact per-token KL(student || teacher) over the sampled tokens.
Because the loss is taken on sequences the student actually produces, and the
target is the base model's own distribution (steered by the expert
demonstration in-context), the update never drags the model onto off-policy
expert tokens the way cross-entropy SFT does — no "destructive" distribution
shift, far less catastrophic forgetting.

Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT) of an open student model (default

## Why not plain SFT?

Cross-entropy on teacher-written tokens is *off-policy*: it forces probability
mass onto sequences the student would never produce itself, dragging the whole
distribution sideways and causing catastrophic forgetting ("destructive SFT").
Classic on-policy distillation (GKD / on-policy KD) fixes this by scoring the
student's *own* rollouts against the teacher's per-token distribution — but the
trace author, `qwen/qwen3.7-max`, is an API model with no logit access.

import torch
from sdft.distill import tokenwise_divergence

torch.manual_seed(0)
s = torch.randn(300, 50, requires_grad=True)
t = torch.randn(300, 50)

# identical distributions -> zero divergence
for kind in ("reverse", "forward", "jsd"):
    z = tokenwise_divergence(s, s.detach(), kind=kind)
    assert z.abs().max() < 1e-5, (kind, z.abs().max())

# different distributions -> positive, grad flows, chunking consistent
d1 = tokenwise_divergence(s, t, kind="reverse", chunk_size=7)
d2 = tokenwise_divergence(s, t, kind="reverse", chunk_size=300)
assert (d1 > 0).all() and torch.allclose(d1, d2, atol=1e-6)
d1.mean().backward()
assert s.grad is not None and s.grad.abs().sum() > 0
print("distill math OK:", d1.shape, float(d1.mean()))
